in a critical overlap system, the difference between DIFS and EIFS has a major impact on the saturation throughput, and that the critical overlap configuration can have higher saturation throughput than the non-overlapping configuration, but only if EIFS>DIFS.

in cochannel cells with overlapping interference ranges, (1) with EIFS>DIFSthere is substantial temporal unfair access between the cells and (2) the critical overlap configuration yields higher per cell throughput compared to the case when the cells have overlapping decoding ranges.

the saturation throughput of a system of two cochannel IEEE 802. 11 WLANs with critical overlap is higher than if the decoding ranges of the cells overlapped and that the throughput of the system is higher if the cells have a larger difference between EIFS and DIFS.

the cochannel cells should have critical overlap, but that the cells should be designed so as to have the same DIFS and EIFS.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in a system of interfering 802.11 cells, the saturation throughputs are maximized if all cells' radio ranges are nonoverlapping and the cells are configured to have the same EIFS and DIFS parameters.
the saturation throughput performance in a multicell WLAN network is a complex function of the number of cells, the cell size, the number of stations in each cell, and the MAC parameters.
the saturation throughput of two cochannel IEEE 802. 11 WLAN cells with critical overlap is higher than the per cell saturation throughput when the cells' decoding regions overlap.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the saturation throughput performance in the critical overlap configuration can be improved by increasing the EIFS value.
the design of the IEEE 802.1 1 MAC protocol parameters should be revisited for multicell WLANs.
, in the design of a large scale IEEE 802.1 1 WLAN system, one must consider not only the number of cells, their radio ranges and the number of nodes per cell, but also the MAC parameter EIFS.
